skill.name: activecampaign-automation
skill.description: Use Rube MCP to manage ActiveCampaign contacts, tags, lists, automation enrollment, and contact tasks with schema-first tool guidance.
skill.summary: Guide ActiveCampaign CRM updates through Rube MCP tool sequences.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static command-execution and reconnaissance alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks and CRM workflow prose, not executable code. The only confirmed issue is the intentional Rube MCP endpoint, which creates a low trust-boundary risk because a third-party service mediates ActiveCampaign operations. No prompt injection or covert data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: External MCP endpoint mediates CRM actions
remediation.suggestion: Document the third-party trust boundary, data sent to Rube MCP, required permissions, and confirmation steps before users run workflows.

content.value_statement: ActiveCampaign updates can be repetitive and error-prone when contacts, tags, lists, automations, and tasks are handled manually. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP tool sequences for those operations.
actual_capabilities: Search for existing ActiveCampaign contacts by email, ID, or phone.
Create contacts with names, phone numbers, organizations, job titles, and tags.
Add or remove contact tags using the required action casing.
Subscribe or unsubscribe contacts from lists using numeric list IDs.
Enroll existing contacts in active automations by email and automation ID.
Create contact tasks with due dates, task type IDs, notes, and assignees.
limitations: Requires an active Rube MCP connection and an authenticated ActiveCampaign account.
Cannot create ActiveCampaign automations; it can only enroll contacts in existing automations.
Some IDs must be found in ActiveCampaign or through separate API access.
Bulk operations still need rate-limit handling and user approval for data changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare new lead records
use_cases.description: Create or update contacts, apply initial tags, and avoid duplicate records before campaign work begins.

use_cases.title: Maintain list membership
use_cases.description: Subscribe or unsubscribe contacts from specific lists while keeping required IDs and action values correct.

use_cases.title: Trigger follow-up workflows
use_cases.description: Enroll contacts in automations and create follow-up tasks for sales or support teams.

prompt_templates.title: Find or create a contact
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ActiveCampaign automation skill to find a contact by email. If the contact does not exist, create it with the details I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Update tags for a segment
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to add these tags to each listed contact. Confirm the action casing and report any contacts that cannot be found.

prompt_templates.title: Manage list subscription status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to subscribe or unsubscribe these contacts from the specified ActiveCampaign list ID. Check for missing emails or contact IDs first.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate automation and tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill to verify each contact, enroll eligible contacts in the target automation, and create dated follow-up tasks for the assigned user.

output_examples.input: Create a contact for Jordan Lee and tag the record as webinar lead.
output_examples.output: The assistant confirms the contact lookup, creates or updates the record, applies the webinar lead tag, and summarizes the final contact status.

output_examples.input: Unsubscribe a customer from list 12 and create a follow-up task for next week.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies the contact, updates the list subscription, creates the task with valid dates, and reports any missing IDs.

output_examples.input: Enroll three existing contacts in automation 45.
output_examples.output: The assistant checks each contact email, enrolls valid contacts in the active automation, and lists contacts needing manual review.

best_practices: Run the Rube tool search first so schemas match the current ActiveCampaign connector.
Confirm contact identity before changing tags, lists, automations, or tasks.
Use small batches with delays when updating many contacts.
anti_patterns: Do not guess list IDs, automation IDs, task type IDs, or assignee IDs.
Do not use this skill without explicit permission to modify CRM records.
Do not mix tag action casing with list subscription action casing.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on Rube MCP and an authenticated ActiveCampaign connection through the active_campaign toolkit.

faq.question: Can it create new automations?
faq.answer: No. It can enroll contacts in existing active automations, but automation creation is handled in ActiveCampaign.

faq.question: Can it create contacts?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create contacts with an email address and optional profile fields or tags.

faq.question: Can it process bulk contact updates?
faq.answer: Yes, for guided batches. Users should add delays and watch ActiveCampaign rate limits.

faq.question: What IDs do users need?
faq.answer: List IDs, automation IDs, task type IDs, contact IDs, and assignee IDs may be required depending on the workflow.

faq.question: Is it safe to run without review?
faq.answer: No. It can change CRM data, so users should review contacts, permissions, and requested changes before execution.
